answers.answer: প্রায় ২০ লক্ষ বছর আগে থেকে প্রায় ১২,০০০ বছর আগে পর্যন্ত
answers.quote: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers 99 per cent of human history.
answers.notes: c11 gives Palaeolithic 2 million to about 12,000 years ago.

answers.answer: তারা শিকার, মাছ ধরা ও বন্য ফল-মূল সংগ্রহ করে খাদ্য জোগাড় করত বলে
answers.quote: Generally, they hunted wild animals, caught fish and birds, gathered fruits, roots, nuts, seeds, leaves, stalks and eggs.
answers.notes: c02 lists hunting, fishing and gathering as food sources; c01 names them hunter-gatherers.

answers.quote: It is likely that people made and used tools of stone, wood and bone, of which stone tools have survived best.
answers.notes: c05: stone tools have survived best.

answers.quote: Traces of ash have been found here. This suggests that people were familiar with the use of fire. Fire could have been used for many things: as a source of light, to roast meat, and to scare away animals.
answers.notes: c10: ash traces at Kurnool caves suggest familiarity with fire.

answers.quote: The period when we find environmental changes, beginning about 12,000 years ago till about 10,000 years ago is called the Mesolithic (middle stone). Stone tools found during this period are generally tiny, and are called microliths.
answers.notes: c12: Mesolithic tiny tools are called microliths.

answers.quote: The first animal to be tamed was the wild ancestor of the dog.
answers.notes: c18: first animal tamed was wild ancestor of the dog.

answers.quote: Some of the earliest plants to be domesticated were wheat and barley. The earliest domesticated animals include sheep and goat.
answers.notes: c21: earliest domesticated animals include sheep and goat.

answers.quote: in Burzahom (in presentday Kashmir) people built pithouses, which were dug into the ground, with steps leading into them. These may have provided shelter in cold weather.
answers.notes: c27: Burzahom in present-day Kashmir.

answers.quote: This site is located in a fertile plain, near the Bolan Pass, which is one of the most important routes into Iran.
answers.notes: c33: Mehrgarh near the Bolan Pass.

answers.quote: Mehrgarh was probably one of the places where people learnt to grow barley and wheat, and rear sheep and goats for the first time in this area. It is one of the earliest villages that we know about.
answers.notes: c34: first learnt to grow barley and wheat at Mehrgarh.

answers.quote: First, if they had stayed at one place for a long time, they would have eaten up all the available plant and animal resources. Therefore, they would have had to go elsewhere in search of food.
answers.notes: c03 (resource exhaustion) and c04 (animal movement, seasonal fruit, water) give the real reasons; building permanent cities is not among them.

answers.quote: Many of the caves in which these early people lived have paintings on the walls. Some of the best examples are from Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar Pradesh. These paintings show wild animals, drawn with great accuracy and skill.
answers.notes: c09: cave paintings show wild animals; c08 places Bhimbetka caves in Madhya Pradesh.

answers.answer: নদী ও হ্রদের মতো জলের উৎসের কাছে
answers.quote: Many sites were located near sources of water, such as rivers and lakes.
answers.notes: c07: many sites near water sources such as rivers and lakes.

answers.quote: Around 12,000 years ago, there were major changes in the climate of the world, with a shift to relatively warm conditions. In many areas, this led to the development of grasslands.
answers.notes: c14: shift to relatively warm conditions led to grasslands.

answers.answer: হরিণ, কৃষ্ণসার, ছাগল, ভেড়া ও গরু
answers.quote: This in turn led to an increase in the number of deer, antelope, goat, sheep and cattle, i.e. animals that survived on grass. Those who hunted these animals now followed them, learning about their food habits and their breeding seasons. It is likely that this helped people to start thinking about herding and rearing these animals themselves. Fishing also became important.
answers.notes: c15 lists deer, antelope, goat, sheep and cattle.

answers.quote: Domestication was a gradual process that took place in many parts of the world. It began about 12,000 years ago.
answers.notes: c20: domestication began about 12,000 years ago.

answers.quote: Some of the earliest plants to be domesticated were wheat and barley. The earliest domesticated animals include sheep and goat.
answers.notes: c21: earliest domesticated plants were wheat and barley.

answers.answer: ফসল পাকা পর্যন্ত গাছের যত্ন — জল দেওয়া, আগাছা তোলা, পশু-পাখি তাড়ানো — করতে হয় বলে
answers.quote: When people began growing plants, it meant that they had to stay in the same place for a long time looking after the plants, watering, weeding, driving away animals and birds — till the grain ripened.
answers.notes: c22: staying to water, weed and drive away animals/birds till grain ripened.

answers.answer: বড় মাটির পাত্র, বোনা ঝুড়ি ও মাটিতে খোঁড়া গর্ত
answers.quote: As grain had to be stored for both food and seed, people had to think of ways of storing it. In many areas, they began making large clay pots, or wove baskets, or dug pits into the ground.
answers.notes: c23: large clay pots, woven baskets, pits dug into the ground.

answers.answer: ঘষে মসৃণ করে ধারালো প্রান্ত দেওয়া হাতিয়ার ও শস্য পেষার শিল-নোড়া
answers.quote: These include tools that were polished to give a fine cutting edge, and mortars and pestles used for grinding grain and other plant produce.
answers.notes: c29: polished fine cutting edge plus mortars and pestles.

answers.answer: ধান, গম ও ডালের মতো শস্য
answers.quote: Many kinds of earthen pots have also been found. These were sometimes decorated, and were used for storing things. People began using pots for cooking food, especially grains like rice, wheat and lentils that now became an important part of the diet.
answers.notes: c30: pots used for cooking grains like rice, wheat and lentils.

answers.quote: Besides, they began weaving cloth, using different kinds of materials, for example cotton, that could now be grown.
answers.notes: c31: weaving cloth using cotton that could now be grown.

answers.answer: বর্গাকার বা আয়তাকার, প্রতিটিতে চার বা তার বেশি কক্ষ
answers.quote: Other finds at Mehrgarh include remains of square or rectangular houses. Each house had four or more compartments, some of which may have been used for storage.
answers.notes: c36: square or rectangular houses, four or more compartments.

answers.quote: Several burial sites have been found at Mehrgarh. In one instance, the dead person was buried with goats, which were probably meant to serve as food in the next world.
answers.notes: c37: dead person buried with goats.

answers.answer: প্রকৃতি থেকে ধাতু নিষ্কাশন, পরিশোধন বা মিশ্রণের কৌশলসহ ধাতুর ধর্মের অধ্যয়ন
answers.quote: Metallurgy: Includes the techniques of extracting metals from nature, purifying or combining them, as well as the scientific study of metals and their properties.
answers.notes: c44 gives the full metallurgy definition.

answers.quote: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers 99 per cent of human history.
answers.notes: c11: Palaeolithic covers 99 per cent of human history.

answers.quote: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers 99 per cent of human history.
answers.notes: c11: divided into Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic (Bengali: nimno, modhyo, uchcho).

answers.answer: কিছু হাতিয়ার মাংস-হাড় কাটা, ছাল-চামড়া চাঁছা ও ফল-শিকড় কুপোনোর কাজে লাগত; কিছু হাতলে লাগিয়ে বর্শা-তীর হত
answers.quote: Some of these stone tools were used to cut meat and bone, scrape bark (from trees) and hides (animal skins), chop fruit and roots. Some may have been attached to handles of bone or wood, to make spears and arrows for hunting.
answers.notes: c06 matches the tool uses and hafting as spears/arrows.

answers.answer: হাড় বা কাঠের হাতলে আটকে করাত, কাস্তের মতো যৌগিক হাতিয়ার হিসেবে
answers.quote: Microliths were probably stuck on to handles of bone or wood to make tools such as saws and sickles. At the same time, older varieties of tools continued to be in use.
answers.notes: c41: microliths stuck on handles to make saws and sickles.

answers.answer: যত্নে রাখলে তারা দুধ দেয় এবং প্রয়োজনে মাংস পাওয়া যায় বলে
answers.quote: Besides, if they are looked after carefully, they provide milk, which is an important source of food, and meat, whenever required. In other words, animals that are reared can be used as a ‘store’ of food.
answers.notes: c24: reared animals provide milk and meat whenever required, a store of food.

answers.answer: আবহাওয়া অনুযায়ী মানুষ ভিতরে বা বাইরে রান্না করতে পারত
answers.quote: Archaeologists have also found cooking hearths both inside and outside the huts, which suggests that, depending on the weather, people could cook food either indoors or outdoors.
answers.notes: c28: hearths inside and outside suggest cooking indoors or outdoors depending on weather.

answers.answer: বদলটা সব জায়গায় একসঙ্গে ঘটেনি; বহু এলাকায় শিকার-সংগ্রহ চলতে থাকে, অন্য জায়গায় কৃষি গৃহীত হয় ধীরে ধীরে কয়েক হাজার বছর ধরে
answers.quote: In many areas, men and women still continued to hunt and gather food, and elsewhere people adopted farming and herding slowly, over several thousand years.
answers.notes: c32: change not everywhere at once; hunting-gathering continued, farming adopted slowly over thousands of years.

answers.answer: এখানকার মানুষ শুরুতে শিকারি ছিল, পরে পশুপালন আরও গুরুত্বপূর্ণ হয়ে ওঠে
answers.quote: At this site many animal bones were found. Bones of wild animals such as the deer and pig, and also bones of sheep and goat were found.
answers.notes: c35 attests both wild (deer, pig) and sheep/goat bones and c34 the first rearing at Mehrgarh; the hunting-to-herding sequence itself is an inference, not stated verbatim in the claims.

answers.quote: Beginning of settlement at Mehrgarh (about 8000 years ago)
answers.notes: c38: beginning of settlement at Mehrgarh about 8000 years ago.

answers.quote: First settlements and beginning of agriculture — 10,000 BCE; Beginning of copper metallurgy — 6000 BCE
answers.notes: c46 timeline: beginning of copper metallurgy about 6000 BCE.

answers.quote: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers 99 per cent of human history.
answers.notes: Order from claims: Palaeolithic begins 2M years ago (c11), Mesolithic about 12,000 years ago (c12), Neolithic about 10,000 years ago (c13), Mehrgarh settlement about 8,000 years ago (c38) = 3,2,4,1.

answers.quote: Domestication was a gradual process that took place in many parts of the world. It began about 12,000 years ago.
answers.notes: Statement 1 true per c20 (domestication began about 12,000 years ago); statement 2 false per c18 (first tamed was dog ancestor, not horse).

answers.quote: in Burzahom (in presentday Kashmir) people built pithouses, which were dug into the ground, with steps leading into them. These may have provided shelter in cold weather.
answers.notes: Statement 1 true per c27 (Burzahom pit-houses); statement 2 true per c29 (polished tools).

answers.quote: Mehrgarh was probably one of the places where people learnt to grow barley and wheat, and rear sheep and goats for the first time in this area. It is one of the earliest villages that we know about.
answers.notes: A-4 Mehrgarh earliest village/first farming (c34), B-2 Burzahom pit-houses (c27), C-1 Kurnool ash/fire (c10), D-3 Bhimbetka cave paintings (c08, c09).

answers.quote: Traces of ash have been found here. This suggests that people were familiar with the use of fire. Fire could have been used for many things: as a source of light, to roast meat, and to scare away animals.
answers.notes: Kurnool caves ash = fire evidence (c10); other pairs misassign Bolan Pass (c33, Mehrgarh), pit-houses (c27, Burzahom) and ash (c10, Kurnool).

answers.answer: A ও R উভয়ই সত্য এবং R, A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: When people began growing plants, it meant that they had to stay in the same place for a long time looking after the plants, watering, weeding, driving away animals and birds — till the grain ripened.
answers.notes: c22 states both A and R and R is the stated reason for staying.

answers.quote: Metallurgy: Includes the techniques of extracting metals from nature, purifying or combining them, as well as the scientific study of metals and their properties.
answers.notes: Statement 2 true per c46 (copper metallurgy about 6000 BCE). Statement 1 is true as far as it goes (c44 includes extraction techniques) but truncates the full definition (also purifying/combining and study of properties), so only-2 is also defensible on a strict reading.
